simple, which is exactly why so many of its real gotchas (mutable defaults,
's trust assumptions) surprise experienced developers coming from other languages, and even Python developers who never pushed past the basics.
Build things. Break things on purpose. Read the standard library. Profile before you optimize. Run
on your own code and see how much it catches. Read a security advisory for a package you use and understand
the fix was necessary, not just that a new version exists.
